blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

faq.a: Yes — land in Big Bend is in the Agricultural Land Reserve administered by the Agricultural Land Commission, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan supports protecting and expanding agriculture there.

faq.q: Is Big Bend in a floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the City states the nearly 800 hectares of low-lying land between Burnaby's south slope and the Fraser River is a floodplain, protected by river and shoreline dykes, pump stations and flood boxes, along nearly 7 km of the North Arm of the Fraser River.

faq.q: What sold in Big Bend in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing — 0 solds from 2 detached listings and 0 solds from 3 condos & townhomes listings, so no sales ratio is applicable and no price conclusion can be drawn from the month. Burnaby-wide, the median detached sale price was $1,825,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $686,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What kinds of properties are in Big Bend?
faq.a: Working farms and nurseries on ALR land, industrial properties on the river employment lands, and rural-residential homes in the Riverside pocket — plus Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park on the river.

faq.q: Is there SkyTrain service in Big Bend?
faq.a: No — there is no station in the district; Big Bend is car- and truck-served, with the town centres and stations of Edmonds and Metrotown up the south slope.
